title: The R API for the mzTab-M File Format
text: mzTab-M format consists four cross-referenced data tables: metadata (MTD), Small Molecule (SML), Small Molecule Feature (SMF) Small Molecule Evidence (SME). MTD section supposed contain experiment measurement relevant information. SML section contains final results analysis reported, .e., (annotated) molecules respective abundances. SMF section contains information measured (LC-MS) features abundance values. SME section contains information annotation process (reliability) molecules reported SML section. SML supposed subset SMF table. structure relationship rows different tables defined mzTab-M standard follows strict rules. functions RmzTabM package assist creating formatting tables.

code: ## Building the mzTab-M metadata information from a `data.frame` with sample ## information of an experiment. Each row in that `data.frame` is one ## measurement of one sample (i.e., represents one *ms_run*). Columns in ## that `data.frame` provide the phenotypic and experimental variables of ## each sample. The example below represents a simple experiment in which ## 3 samples (e.g. cell lines) were measured. Columns *time_point and ## *cell_count* provide the time point (in hours) when samples were ## collected and the number of cells per sample. In addition, one ## sample has the genotype *WT* and two *KO*. Column `"operator"` contains ## the initials of the researcher extracting the samples exp <- data.frame(     sample_name = c("S1_T1", "S1_T2", "S2_T1", "S2_T2", "S3_T1", "S3_T2"),     sample_id = c("S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3"),     time_point = c(0, 6, 0, 6, 0, 6),     cell_count = c(13000, 8700, 10100, 6000, 14000, 4500),     genotype = c("WT", "WT", "KO", "KO", "KO", "KO"),     operator = c("BB", "BB", "BB", "BB", "FB", "FB"),     file_name = c("s1-t1.mzML", "s1-t2.mzML", "s2-t1.mzML", "s2-t2.mzML",                   "s3-t1.mzML", "s3-t2.mzML") ) exp #>   sample_name sample_id time_point cell_count genotype operator  file_name #> 1       S1_T1        S1          0      13000       WT       BB s1-t1.mzML #> 2       S1_T2        S1          6       8700       WT       BB s1-t2.mzML #> 3       S2_T1        S2          0      10100       KO       BB s2-t1.mzML #> 4       S2_T2        S2          6       6000       KO       BB s2-t2.mzML #> 5       S3_T1        S3          0      14000       KO       FB s3-t1.mzML #> 6       S3_T2        S3          6       4500       KO       FB s3-t2.mzML   ############################################################################# ## Core metadata information  ## We first compile the general metadata information. title: Export a mzTab-M 2.1 file — MzTabM-export
text: Write validate mzTab-M (version 2.1) file. writer recognises four standard sections: MTD (Metadata): Always required. metadata section provides additional information dataset(s) reported mzTab-M 2.1 file. SML (Small Molecule Summary): Optional. row small molecule section intended report one final result communicated terms molecule quantified. SMF (Small Molecule Feature): Optional required SME section present. small molecule feature section represents individual MS regions measured/quantified. SMF row represent single isotopomer. SME (Small Molecule Evidence): Optional. small molecule evidence section represents evidence identifications small molecules/features. typical case, row represents one result single search intepretation piece evidence. Column names SMH, SFH SEH used section headers.

title: Export a mzTab-M 2.1 file — MzTabM-export
code: ## Basic usage exp <- data.frame(     sample_name = c("S1_T1", "S1_T2", "S2_T1", "S2_T2", "S3_T1", "S3_T2"),     sample_id = c("S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3"),     timepoint = c("0h", "6h", "0h", "6h", "0h", "6h"),     genotype = c("WT", "WT", "KO", "KO", "KO", "KO"),     operator = c("BB", "BB", "BB", "BB", "FB", "FB"),     file_name = c("s1-t1.mzML", "s1-t2.mzML", "s2-t1.mzML", "s2-t2.mzML",                  "s3-t1.mzML", "s3-t2.mzML") ) mtd <- mtdSkeleton(id = "EXP_1", software = "[MS, MS:1001582, xcms, 4.1.0]")  mtd_s <- mtdSample(sample = unique(exp$sample_id)) mtd <- rbind(mtd, mtd_s)  mtd_msr <- mtdMsRun(     location = exp$file_name,     format = "[MS, MS:1000584, mzML file, ]",     id_format = "[MS, MS:1000530, mzML unique identifier, ]",     scan_polarity = "positive") mtd <- rbind(mtd, mtd_msr)  mtd_a <- mtdAssay(     assay = exp$sample_name,     sample_ref = c("sample[1]", "sample[1]", "sample[2]", "sample[2]",                    "sample[3]", "sample[3]"),     ms_run_ref = paste0("ms_run[", seq_len(nrow(exp)), "]") ) mtd <- rbind(mtd, mtd_a)  mtd_svar <- mtdStudyVariables(     exp, groups = c("timepoint", "genotype", "operator"),     group_unit = c("[, , hours, ]", "", "")) mtd <- rbind(mtd, mtd_svar) mtd <- mtdSort(mtd)  x <- list("MTD" = mtd) filepath <- file.path(tempdir(), "example.mztab")  result <- writeMzTabM(x, path = filepath)  ## Add comments comments <- c("Test comment") results <- writeMzTabM(x, path = filepath, comments = comments)

title: Import a mzTab-M 2.1 file — MzTabM-import
text: Reads parses mzTab-M (version 2.1) file MzTabM object. parser recognises four standard sections: MTD (Metadata): Always required. metadata section provides additional information dataset(s) reported mzTab-M 2.1 file. SML (Small Molecule Summary): Optional. row small molecule section intended report one final result communicated terms molecule quantified. SMF (Small Molecule Feature): Optional required SME section present. small molecule feature section represents individual MS regions measured/quantified. SMF row represent single isotopomer. SME (Small Molecule Evidence): Optional. small molecule evidence section represents evidence identifications small molecules/features. typical case, row represents one result single search intepretation piece evidence. Section headers (SMH, SFH, SEH) used column names respective data sections. MTD section dedicated header row; two-column key–value structure returned without column names.

The mapping between the MTD fields ## and the column names in `colData()` can be configured with parameters ## `sampleCols.`, `msRunCols.` and `assayCols.`. We use the respective ## helper functions to define these mappings:  ## We use available `colData()` columns `"sample_name"`, `"species"` and ## `"tissue"` for the MTD sample fields *sample*, *species* and *tissue*: s_cols <- sampleCols(sample = "sample_name", species = "species",     tissue = "tissue")  ## We use `colData()` columns `"derived_spectra_data_file"` for *location* ## (i.e., the originating MS data file) and `"polarity"` for the ## *scan_polarity* field: m_cols <- msRunCols(location = "derived_spectra_data_file",     scan_polarity = "polarity")  ## For the present data set one MS run corresponds to one *assay*, hence we ## use also the MS data file name for the MTD field *assay*: a_cols <- assayCols(assay = "derived_spectra_data_file")  ## For the experimental design we use columns `"phenotype"` and `"age"`, ## which we provide with parameter `groups`. Having all these parameters ## defined we create now a `MzTabM` from the `SummarizedExperiment`: m <- MzTabM(se, id = "MTBLS8735", sampleCols. = s_cols, msRunCols. = m_cols,     assayCols. = a_cols, groups = c("phenotype", "age")) m #> Object of class MzTabM #> mzTab-M version 2.1.0-M #>  MTD section with 149 rows. head(mtd(m)) #>                              #> [1,] "mzTab-version"         #> [2,] "mzTab-ID"              #> [3,] "software[1]"           #> [4,] "quantification_method" #> [5,] "sample[1]"             #> [6,] "sample[1]-species[1]"  #>      values                                                       #> [1,] "2.1.0-M"                                                    #> [2,] "MTBLS8735"                                                  #> [3,] "[,,RmzTabM,RmzTabM version 0.99.1]"                         #> [4,] "[MS, MS:1001834, LC-MS label-free quantitation analysis, ]" #> [5,] "POOL"                                                       #> [6,] "[NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]"                 ## Importantly, depending on the provided information, the MTD section might ## be needed to be completed. See also the help for `MzTabM` for more ## information and helper functions to add/replace metadata content.  ############################################################################# ## Create a `MzTabM` with MTD + SMF  ## We need to specify which columns in the `SummarizedExperiment`'s ## `rowData()` contain information characterizing the individual features. colnames(rowData(se)) #>  [1] "mzmed"    "mzmin"    "mzmax"    "rtmed"    "rtmin"    "rtmax"    #>  [7] "npeaks"   "CTR"      "CVD"      "QC"       "ms_level"  ## - *mzmed* defines the features *m/z* value and can be mapped to the SMF ##   field (column) *exp_mass_to_charge*. ## - *rtmed* reports the median retention time of the feature and can be ##   used for the SMF field *retention_time_in_seconds*. ## We will in addition add an optional field *feature_id* to report and add ## the IDs of the individual features from the `SummarizedExperiment`: ## add a column `"feature_id"` to the `rowData()` rowData(se)$feature_id <- rownames(se)  ## Define the mapping of SMF fields to `rowData()` columns: smf_cols <- smfCols(exp_mass_to_charge = "mzmed",     retention_time_in_seconds = "rtmed", feature_id = "feature_id")  ## We can use the `smf()` function to create the SMF section. For the ## SMF abundances we use the data from the `"raw_filled"` assay assayNames(se) #> [1] "raw"        "raw_filled"  tmp <- smf(se, assayName = "raw_filled", smfCols. = smf_cols) head(tmp) #> title: mzTab-M assay metadata information — mtdAssay
text: mtdAssay() function assists compiling assay information metadata section. assay must associated least one entry ms_run section (see mtdMsRun()). mapping can defined ms_run_ref parameter providing ID/name run (e.g. "ms_run[1]"). Important: support optional additional parameters passed along ... parameters (assay, sample_ref etc) fully spelled . details expected input various parameter strongly suggested consult mzTab-M documentation.

title: mzTab-M assay metadata information — mtdAssay
code: mtdAssay(   ...,   assay = character(),   external_uri = character(),   sample_ref = character(),   ms_run_ref = character(),   protocol_ref = character(),   parameters = character() )

title: mzTab-M assay metadata information — mtdAssay
text: ... optional additional (custom) parameters assay. provided, length character vector(s) match length parameter assay. assay character names assay(s). assay must reported following sections (e.g. SMF section). external_uri optional character reference information assay, example via reference object within ISA-TAB file. Can length 1 (case reference assigned every assay) length equal length assay. sample_ref optional character ID/name sample assay (e.g. "sample[1]"). provided, length match length assay. ms_run_ref character ID associated ms_run(s). multiplexed assays, different assays can refer run. support pre-fractionated samples, also possible provide list character runs assay measured . See examples details. protocol_ref optional character ID/name protocol assay (e.g. "protocol[1]"). provided, length match length assay. parameters optional character additional parameters assay.

title: mzTab-M assay metadata information — mtdAssay
text: two-column character matrix content assay metadata section.

code: ## Defining an example sample data: ## - file: the mzML file, i.e., the *MS run*. ## - name: the name of the measurement. This is also the name of the sample: ##         QC is the pool of all samples, s1 to s4 the ID of the individual. ## - phenotype: defining the biological replicates, 2 for CVD, 2 for CTR. ## - age: covariate, age of the individuals. ## - injection_index: the order in which samples were measured. sdata <- data.frame(     file = c("1.mzML", "2.mzML", "3.mzML", "4.mzML", "5.mzML", "6.mzML"),     name = c("QC", "s1", "s2", "QC", "s3", "s4"),     phenotype = c(NA, "CVD", "CTR", NA, "CTR", "CVD"),     age = c(NA, 35, 32, NA, 43, 32),     injection_index = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)) ## Add additional required columns: sdata$polarity <- "positive"  ## Add columns with optional, additional information to the individual ## samples or assays. sdata$organism <- "[NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]" sdata$assay_info <- c("run1", "run2", "run3", "run4", "run5", "run6")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide information on the individual ## samples. scols <- sampleCols(sample = "name", species = "organism")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide MS run information mscols <- msRunCols(location = "file", scan_polarity = "polarity")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide assay information; we use ## the MS run/file name also for the assay name and add an additional ## column with optional content/information. acols <- assayCols(assay = "file", assay_info = "assay_info")  ## Create the MTD section from the `sdata` `data.frame`. Parameter `groups` ## allows to define the columns in `sdata` that should be encoded as ## *study variable groups*. m <- mtdFromSampleData(sdata, sampleCols = scols, msRunCols = mscols,     assayCols = acols, groups = c("phenotype", "age", "injection_index"))  ## The sample to assay mapping: ## The repeated injection (assay 1 and 4) of the QC sample are assigned ## to the same sample (1). getMtdField(m, "assay\\[\\d\\]-sample_ref") #> assay[1]-sample_ref assay[2]-sample_ref assay[3]-sample_ref assay[4]-sample_ref  #>         "sample[1]"         "sample[2]"         "sample[3]"         "sample[1]"  #> assay[5]-sample_ref assay[6]-sample_ref  #>         "sample[4]"         "sample[5]"   ## The study variable 2 represents a value of `"CVD"` for the *phenotype* ## study variable group getMtdField(m, "study_variable\\[2\\]$") #> study_variable[2]  #>             "CVD"   ## and this study variable references the 2nd and 6th assay getMtdField(m, "study_variable\\[2\\]-assay_refs") #> study_variable[2]-assay_refs  #>          "assay[2]|assay[6]"    ## It is also possible to create a MTD section without samples or ## study variables m <- mtdFromSampleData(     sdata,     msRunCols = c(location = "file", scan_polarity = "polarity"),     assayCols = c(assay = "assay_info")) m #>                                                    #>  [1,] "ms_run[1]-location" "ms_run[5]-location"                         #> [10,] "ms_run[5]-scan_polarity[1]"                 #> [11,] "ms_run[6]-location"                         #> [12,] "ms_run[6]-scan_polarity[1]" "assay[4]-ms_run_ref"                        #> [21,] "assay[5]"                                   #> [22,] "assay[5]-ms_run_ref"                        #> [23,] "assay[6]" "study_variable[1]-description"              #>       values                                                  #>  [1,] "1.mzML"                                                #>  [2,] "[MS, text: Gabriele Tomè

title: Reconstruct a sample data frame from mzTab-M MTD content — mtdToSampleData
code: ## Defining an example sample data: ## - file: the mzML file, i.e., the *MS run*. ## - name: the name of the measurement. This is also the name of the sample: ##         QC is the pool of all samples, s1 to s4 the ID of the individual. ## - phenotype: defining the biological replicates, 2 for CVD, 2 for CTR. ## - age: covariate, age of the individuals. ## - injection_index: the order in which samples were measured. sdata <- data.frame(     file = c("1.mzML", "2.mzML", "3.mzML", "4.mzML", "5.mzML", "6.mzML"),     name = c("QC", "s1", "s2", "QC", "s3", "s4"),     phenotype = c(NA, "CVD", "CTR", NA, "CTR", "CVD"),     age = c(NA, 35, 32, NA, 43, 32),     injection_index = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)) ## Add additional required columns: sdata$polarity <- "positive"  ## Add columns with optional, additional information to the individual ## samples or assays. sdata$organism <- "[NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]" sdata$assay_info <- c("run1", "run2", "run3", "run4", "run5", "run6")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide information on the individual ## samples. scols <- sampleCols(sample = "name", species = "organism")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide MS run information mscols <- msRunCols(location = "file", scan_polarity = "polarity")  ## Define the columns in `sdata` that provide assay information; we use ## the MS run/file name also for the assay name and add an additional ## column with optional content/information. acols <- assayCols(assay = "file", assay_info = "assay_info")  ## Create the MTD section from the `sdata` `data.frame`. Parameter `groups` ## allows to define the columns in `sdata` that should be encoded as ## *study variable groups*. m <- mtdFromSampleData(sdata, sampleCols = scols, msRunCols = mscols,     assayCols = acols, groups = c("phenotype", "age", "injection_index"))  ## Reconstruct the sample data from the MTD section. The column names might ## differ from the original `sdata` `data.frame` if non-mzTabM names are ## used in the original sdata, but the content is identical. sdata2 <- mtdToSampleData(m) sdata2 #>              id sample_ref ms_run_ref  assay            custom.1. location #> 1.mzML assay[1]  sample[1]  ms_run[1] 1.mzML [,,assay_info, run1]   1.mzML #> 2.mzML assay[2]  sample[2]  ms_run[2] 2.mzML [,,assay_info, run2]   2.mzML #> 3.mzML assay[3]  sample[3]  ms_run[3] 3.mzML [,,assay_info, run3]   3.mzML #> 4.mzML assay[4]  sample[1]  ms_run[4] 4.mzML [,,assay_info, run4]   4.mzML #> 5.mzML assay[5]  sample[4]  ms_run[5] 5.mzML [,,assay_info, run5]   5.mzML #> 6.mzML assay[6]  sample[5]  ms_run[6] 6.mzML [,,assay_info, run6]   6.mzML #>                         scan_polarity.1. sample #> 1.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     QC #> 2.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     s1 #> 3.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     s2 #> 4.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     QC #> 5.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     s3 #> 6.mzML [MS, MS:1000130, positive scan, ]     s4 #>                                         species.1. injection_index phenotype #> 1.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               1      <NA> #> 2.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               2       CVD #> 3.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               3       CTR #> 4.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               4      <NA> #> 5.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               5       CTR #> 6.mzML [NCBITaxon, NCBITaxon:9606, Homo sapiens, ]               6       CVD #>         age #> 1.mzML <NA> #> 2.mzML   35 #> 3.mzML   32 #> 4.mzML <NA> #> 5.mzML   43 #> 6.mzML   32

title: Utility functions for CV parameters — parseCvParameter
text: mzTab-M makes use controlled vocabulary (CV) parameters. parameters expected provided format "[CV label, accession, name, value]". addition, also user parameters name value provided supported, recommendet use full CV parameters possible. parseCvParameter() allows extract individual fields CV parameter. isCvParameter() tests whether string expected (CV parameter) format.

Details settings preprocessing provided Metabonaut resource (end--end metabolomics data analysis workflow) Louail et al.; Zenodo. data set contains two abundance matrices (assays): "raw": original quantified feature abunances representing integrated peak areas identified chromatographic peaks. "raw_filled": gap-filled feature abundance matrix. content assay "raw" missing values replaced MS signal measured expected peak area respective ions/features.

title: Add or Update contact Metadata of an mzTab-M MTD section — setMtdContact
text: x MTD section stores metadata fields. Can two-column character matrix, two-column data.frame MzTabM() object. Defaults matrix(). values NA, function returns x unchanged. name character contact’s name. affiliation character contact’s affiliation. email character contact’s e-mail address. orcid character contact’s ORCID identifier. replace logical flag controlling pre-existing contact metadata handled: FALSE (default): new values appended existing values. TRUE: existing instrument metadata discarded replaced entirely supplied arguments.

text: x MTD section stores metadata fields. Can two-column character matrix, two-column data.frame MzTabM() object. Defaults matrix(). values NA, function returns x unchanged. label character describing labels controlled vocabularies/ontologies used mzTab-M file (e.g. "MS" PSI-MS). full_name character describing full names controlled vocabularies/ontologies used. version character describing version controlled vocabularies/ontologies used. (e.g. "4.1.11") uri character containing URIs controlled vocabularies/ ontologies used mzTab file.
